name: Yangarra Estate Grenache High Sands 2014
text:
## Yangarra Estate Grenache High Sands 2014

**The story.** Yangarra Estate is a single-vineyard estate in Blewitt Springs, at the northern edge of [McLaren Vale](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Yangarra+Estate+Vineyard,+McLaren+Flat+Road,+Kangarilla,+South+Australia,+Australia&t=k), the wine region south of Adelaide between the [Gulf St Vincent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_St_Vincent) and the [Mount Lofty Ranges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Lofty_Ranges) ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Vale)). McLaren Vale is one of Australia's oldest wine regions: John Reynell and Thomas Hardy planted vines there from 1838. Yangarra itself began as the Eringa Park vineyard, bought in 2000 by California's [Jackson Family Wines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_Family_Wines), of [Kendall-Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendall-Jackson) fame, and renamed ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_Family_Wines)).

Yangarra is devoted to the grapes of the southern [Rhône](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rh%C3%B4ne_wine), with old bush-vine [Grenache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenache) as its cornerstone and rarer varieties such as Bourboulenc, Picpoul Noir, Clairette and [Counoise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counoise); it was the first in Australia to plant [Grenache Blanc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenache_blanc) commercially ([Yangarra](https://www.yangarra.com/pages/about-yangarra-estate)). The estate began converting in 2008 and has been certified [biodynamic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodynamic_agriculture) and organic since 2012: no synthetic herbicides, pesticides or fertilisers, biodynamic preparations made with cow horns, quartz and herbs, and sheep grazing between the vines in winter ([Yangarra](https://www.yangarra.com/pages/our-vineyard)). In the cellar it uses wild fermentation, basket presses, ceramic eggs, amphorae and large oak foudres ([Yangarra](https://www.yangarra.com/pages/wines-and-winemaking)).

**The wine: High Sands.** High Sands is "the pinnacle of our estate": a single-block Grenache from bush vines planted in 1946, "reaching deep within the sandy soil", made in tiny quantities and today sold only to Yangarra's wine club and loyalty members ([Yangarra](https://www.yangarra.com/pages/high-sands-grenache)). For the 2014, Halliday's Wine Companion describes fruit from Block 31, the highest part of the vineyard at 210 metres with the deepest sand; 50% whole berries, wild yeast, and a year on lees in used French oak, at 14.5% alcohol ([Nicks Wine Merchants, critics' notes](https://www.nicks.com.au/products/2014-yangarra-high-sands-grenache)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [South Australia vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/south-australia) says 2014 saw "everything from frost to high winds to heatwaves", with yields lower than usual; "nobody is claiming it is a great vintage", but quality is generally reliable. The critics loved this wine all the same.

**What the critics say for 2014.** As listed by [Nicks Wine Merchants](https://www.nicks.com.au/products/2014-yangarra-high-sands-grenache):
- **Jane Faulkner, [James Halliday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Halliday_%28writer%29)'s Wine Companion: 97**. "A pure expression of that discrete spot", with no need for "winemaking accoutrements"; perfectly modulated tannins, the most savoury, earthy and deepest of Yangarra's three Grenaches. Drink by 2034.
- **Gary Walsh, The Wine Front: 96+**. "This is stunning Grenache": fresh field roses, raspberry, aniseed, dried mint and almost chocolate; medium-bodied, with sweet fine-grained tannin, "not confected or gooey in any sense". Hard to choose between the 2013 and 2014: "the latter all grace and charm". He "could even twist my arm to 97". Drink 2020 to 2037.
- **Nicks Wine Merchants: 97** (May 2020), the retailer's own score: black raspberry, dark cherry and licorice, "outstanding power finishing exceptionally long".
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 92.6** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is twelve years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2021 to 2031, and the critics' windows run to 2034 and 2037. So it is in its prime: perfumed, savoury Grenache with roses, raspberry, spice and earth. Serve it slightly cool, at about 15 to 16°C, and decant it for about an hour.

**Food.** Grenache like this suits Mediterranean food: roast lamb with garlic and rosemary, a [tagine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagine), duck with cherries, roast pork belly, or grilled mushrooms. My pick for a perfumed, earthy 2014: slow-roasted lamb shoulder with olives and thyme.

**Value and where to buy.** High Sands is sold mainly through the estate's own allocation, so it rarely reaches stores. But Yangarra's other wines are easy to find here: BSW Liquor has the Old Vine Grenache 2023 and GSM at $42.99 and the Shiraz at $36, and ZYN has the McLaren Vale Grenache 2022 at $37.80, the GSM at $40.50 and the Shiraz at $37.20.

**From the history books**
- **Named for a McLaren.** McLaren Vale was named after either David McLaren, Colonial Manager of the South Australian Company, or John McLaren, who surveyed the area in 1839. The first settlers grew cereal crops, but John Reynell and Thomas Hardy planted vines in 1838, and the forerunners of today's Seaview and Hardys wineries were running by 1850 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Vale)).
- **Century-old vines.** Some McLaren Vale vines more than 100 years old are still producing ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Vale)), and the region is a member of the Great Wine Capitals of the World network.
- **Between the gulf and the hills.** The region runs 30 km down the coast of the [Gulf St Vincent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_St_Vincent) to the foothills of the [Mount Lofty Ranges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Lofty_Ranges), with a [Mediterranean climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_climate) of four clear seasons ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Vale)).
- **Penfolds comes south.** Between 1904 and 1912 [Penfolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penfolds), then the largest winery around Adelaide, bought vineyards in McLaren Vale ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penfolds)).

**Curious details**
- **Sheep in the vineyard.** Sheep graze the vines through winter, keeping the grass down and fertilising the soil without tractors ([Yangarra](https://www.yangarra.com/pages/our-vineyard)).
- **Quartz in a cow horn.** Biodynamic preparation 501 is ground quartz buried in cow horns over summer and sprayed on the vines, which Yangarra says aids light and photosynthesis ([Yangarra](https://www.yangarra.com/pages/our-vineyard)).
- **Kings' oak.** Yangarra's foudres are made of French oak from royal forests, planted by monarchs to build cathedrals and church naves ([Yangarra](https://www.yangarra.com/pages/wines-and-winemaking)).
